Add Raw UMI Counts to $cell.data

Source: R/add_cell_rawcounts.R
add_cell_rawcounts.Rd

Adds a count column to niches.obj$cell.data from a user-supplied gene x cell raw count matrix. The count column records the original sequencing depth for each (cell, gene) pair as a provenance record; it is not used by any other NICHESv2 function.

Usage

add_cell_rawcounts(niches.obj, count.mtx, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject.

count.mtx

A gene x cell raw count matrix. Either a base matrix or a sparse Matrix object (e.g., dgCMatrix). Must have rownames (gene symbols) and colnames (cell barcodes) covering every cell in niches.obj$cell.list.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), emits messages for missing genes, new rows added, and an overwrite notice if a count column already exists.

Value

Updated NICHESObject with a count column in $cell.data. Row count may increase if any (cell, gene) pairs had count > 0 and score = 0.

Row expansion

$cell.data is sparse: it originally contains only (cell, gene) pairs where score > 0. When raw counts are provided, new rows are appended for any (cell, gene) pair where count > 0 but score = 0 (e.g., a gene detected in sequencing but not expressed in the scoring layer). New rows carry score = 0 and score.norm = 0.

Gene coverage

count.mtx must cover every cell in niches.obj$cell.list (hard error if any are missing). Genes in niches.obj$gene.list absent from rownames(count.mtx) receive count = NA with a message when verbose = TRUE. Extra rows in count.mtx not in $gene.list are silently ignored.

Validation

Non-zero stored values are checked for validity. Warnings (not errors) are emitted if any values are negative or non-integer; the pipeline continues regardless. These checks help detect accidental use of a normalized layer instead of raw counts.

See also

create_NICHESObject for object construction; extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat and extract_NICHESInputs_AnnData for obtaining a count matrix from Seurat or AnnData objects.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_inputs)
data(NICHESv2_example)

# NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx is the raw count matrix used to build
# NICHESv2_example. Attach it as the provenance count column.
obj <- add_cell_rawcounts(NICHESv2_example, NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
head(obj$cell.data[, c("cell", "gene", "score", "score.norm", "count")])
#> Key: <cell, gene>
#>      cell   gene score score.norm count
#>    <char> <char> <num>      <num> <num>
#> 1: Cell_1 Gene10     7 0.10606061     7
#> 2: Cell_1 Gene11     6 0.09090909     6
#> 3: Cell_1 Gene12     2 0.03030303     2
#> 4: Cell_1 Gene25     5 0.07575758     5
#> 5: Cell_1 Gene33     6 0.09090909     6
#> 6: Cell_1  Gene4     8 0.12121212     8
# }
